mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the past month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or if the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the past month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the consumer price index is rising faster than 2% annually, the combined effect of high interest rates and inflationary pressure typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3%, this dual signal of a strengthening labor market typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts by more than 10% in the past month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing market is a leading indicator of broader economic demand.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between HOUST decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Real personal consumption expenditures rising faster than 0.5% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as increased consumer spending boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of periods with rising RSAFS, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
